article.headline: The Canonical X Finance Picks List Arrives, Right on Schedule
article.lede: Every year, the same ritual: a roster of speculative small-caps — this time satellites, rockets, AI data centers, and drones — packaged as a life-changing picks list. The genre is as reliable as earnings season, and nearly as predictable.
article.body:
There is a recognisable grammar to the annual stock-picks thread on X. It arrives between December and May, runs to a tidy ten names, promises millionaire-making returns from the prior year's edition, and clusters around whichever technology narrative currently commands the most retail attention. For 2026, that narrative is three overlapping waves: the commercialisation of low-Earth orbit, artificial-intelligence infrastructure, and the pivot of cryptocurrency mining operations into AI data-centre hosts. @MrMikeInvesting's list — Ondas Holdings ($ONDS), AST SpaceMobile ($ASTS), Rocket Lab ($RKLB), IREN Limited ($IREN), and Nebius Group ($NBIS), among others — is a near-perfect specimen of the form.

The most credible name on the list is also the one that has already done the heavy lifting for patient shareholders. Rocket Lab reported 2025 revenue of roughly $630 million and a backlog of $1.85 billion — a 73 per cent year-on-year increase — while completing 21 Electron launches with a perfect success record. Its shares rose approximately 174 per cent in 2025 and roughly 1,775 per cent over three years, which raises the obvious question: how much of the story is priced in? The company's medium-lift *Neutron* rocket, its next major growth vector, suffered a tank rupture during testing and has been pushed to late 2026 or early 2027. An $816 million Space Development Agency contract for satellite work has refreshed analyst enthusiasm, but the stock has already compounded into a valuation that demands execution.

AST SpaceMobile is the list's most genuinely novel idea. The company's *BlueBird* satellite constellation aims to beam broadband directly to standard smartphones — no special hardware required — a technically audacious goal that, if achieved, would upend rural and emerging-market telecoms. Full-year 2025 revenue reached $70.9 million, its first meaningful commercial figure, backed by over $1.2 billion in contracted commitments from carrier partners. The satellite-deployment cadence is the critical variable: a New Glenn launch anomaly cost the company one *BlueBird* unit, leaving it perhaps seven satellites short of its end-2026 target of 45 to 60. The gap between the ambition and the orbital tally is where risk lives.

IREN Limited and Nebius Group represent a newer archetype: companies that began somewhere else and are now racing toward AI infrastructure. IREN, formerly Iris Energy, was a bitcoin miner that pivoted aggressively into liquid-cooled, high-performance computing data centres after securing Nvidia preferred-partner status in 2024. Its shares rose roughly 285 per cent in 2025, propelled by a major Microsoft contract and guidance for $3.4 billion in annualised recurring revenue by end-2026. Nebius, carved out of the wreckage of the Russian internet giant Yandex after the invasion of Ukraine, has emerged as an improbable AI-cloud challenger, reporting $530 million in 2025 revenue — up 479 per cent year-on-year — and announcing a contracted backlog approaching $50 billion anchored by deals with Microsoft and Meta. At roughly 47 times trailing sales, it is a stock that requires one to believe the future has already arrived.

Ondas Holdings, the quietest name on the list, operates in a different register altogether: private wireless networks and autonomous drone systems for rail, utilities, and defence. Revenue of $50.7 million in 2025 represented 605 per cent growth, driven by acquisitions rather than organic demand, while losses widened to $137 million. The company has guided for $375 million in 2026 revenue and rebranded as Ondas Inc. in January — a rebrand being, in the taxonomy of micro-cap promotion, both an encouraging sign of ambition and a flag worth noting.

The asymmetry of a list like this is worth naming plainly. Five names are visible; the bottom five are withheld, a common device that creates scarcity and social-media engagement without accountability. More tellingly, several picks — Rocket Lab, IREN, Nebius — had already delivered multi-bagger returns *before* the list was published, meaning new followers entering at list-publication prices bear a substantially different risk profile than those who held through the prior year. The genre does not advertise this distinction. The companies themselves may well be legitimate; the frame in which they are delivered is the thing to interrogate.
article.fact_check: The claim that "many millionaires were made" from prior picks lists is unverifiable and a common promotional assertion in the genre. No audited track record is publicly available for @MrMikeInvesting. Underlying data points used in the body — revenue figures, backlog numbers, stock-price returns, satellite counts — are drawn from company filings and financial news sources and are cited accordingly.

ticker_onds.name: Ondas Holdings, Inc.
ticker_onds.blurb: Ondas Holdings is an autonomous systems and drone technology company operating through two main segments: Ondas Autonomous Systems (drone and counter-drone platforms) and Ondas Networks (industrial wireless communications). Its Iron Drone Raider counter-UAS system and Optimus autonomous drone platforms serve defence, homeland security, and industrial customers in the US, Europe, Israel, and the UAE.
ticker_onds.recent: Ondas delivered 605% revenue growth in 2025, with Q4 2025 revenue of $30.1 million — up 629% year-over-year. A pending $175 million merger with Mistral, a Bethesda, MD-based prime contractor with over $1 billion in existing DoD IDIQ (indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity) contracts, was announced. The company secured US border-security drone contracts. Stock rallied over 1,000% from 52-week lows, driven by defence-drone demand and the Mistral deal, before analysts cautioned on execution risk at elevated multiples.

ticker_asts.name: AST SpaceMobile, Inc.
ticker_asts.blurb: AST SpaceMobile is building a network of large-aperture satellites in low Earth orbit designed to deliver broadband directly to unmodified standard mobile handsets — no specialised hardware required. The company has carrier partnerships representing roughly three billion potential subscribers, including AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone, and Rakuten, and secured $1 billion in hard commercial commitments from those partners.
ticker_asts.recent: BlueBird 6, described as the largest commercial communications array ever deployed in LEO, launched aboard an ISRO LVM3 rocket in December 2025. The company targets intermittent US nationwide service in early 2026 and continuous service by late 2026, with 45-60 satellites on orbit by year-end. A 10-year commercial agreement with stc Group (Saudi Arabia) was signed in October 2025.

ticker_rklb.description: Long Beach, California-based vertically integrated space and defense company. Operates two primary business lines: Launch Services (Electron small-sat rocket, HASTE hypersonic test vehicle) and Space Systems (satellite design and manufacture, spacecraft components including solar panels, reaction wheels, star trackers, and radios). Electron, the world's most frequently launched privately-developed small rocket, completed 21 missions in 2025 with a 100% success rate. Developing Neutron, a partially reusable medium-lift rocket targeted for first launch in Q4 2026 or early 2027.
key_facts: Full Year 2025 revenue: $602M (+38% YoY); Q4 2025 revenue: $180M (record); GAAP gross margin Q4: 37.9%
Record backlog: $1.85B at end-2025 (+73% YoY); cash position $829M (from $271M in 2024)
Net loss FY2025: $198M; company profitable at gross margin level but not yet at operating income level
Q1 2026 guidance: $185–200M revenue (+57% YoY); non-GAAP gross margin 39–41%; adj. EBITDA loss $21–27M
December 2025: $816M SDA contract to build 18 satellites for Tracking Layer Tranche 3 missile-warning constellation — largest ever single contract
HASTE hypersonic test program: $190M block-buy for 20 suborbital flights under MACH-TB 2.0; also onramped to multi-billion NSSL Phase 3 launch services pool

Neutron development: first launch targeted Q4 2026 after Stage 1 tank rupture during qualification (manufacturing defect in hand-laid autoclave joint); ~$360M cumulative program spend through end-2025
Archimedes engine (methane/LOx, 1.5M lbf aggregate thrust on Neutron first stage) testing 20 hrs/day, 7 days/week at NASA Stennis
21 Electron launches in 2025 — 100% mission success rate; cumulative Electron launch count exceeded 70
52-week range: $20.23–$99.58; all-time closing high $96.30 on January 16, 2026
200-day MA ~$68; 50-day MA ~$72 (as of early May 2026) — stock trading above both
Analyst consensus: 9 Buy, 5 Hold, 1 Sell (17 analysts); mean price target ~$83

ticker_rklb.blurb: Rocket Lab Corporation is a Long Beach, California-based vertically integrated space and defense company. It operates two primary business lines: Launch Services (Electron small-sat rocket, HASTE hypersonic test vehicle) and Space Systems (satellite design and manufacture, spacecraft components including solar panels, reaction wheels, star trackers, and radios). Electron, the world's most frequently launched privately-developed small rocket, completed 21 missions in 2025 with a 100% success rate. The company is developing Neutron, a partially reusable medium-lift rocket targeted for first launch in Q4 2026 or early 2027.
ticker_rklb.recent: Full-year 2025 revenue was $602 million (+38% YoY) on a record $1.85 billion backlog (+73% YoY), with a $198 million net loss; Q1 2026 guidance calls for $185–200 million revenue (+57% YoY). In December 2025 Rocket Lab won an $816 million SDA contract to build 18 satellites for the Tracking Layer Tranche 3 missile-warning constellation — its largest ever single contract — and the HASTE hypersonic test program now carries a $190 million block-buy for 20 suborbital flights under MACH-TB 2.0. Neutron development continues at NASA Stennis after a Stage 1 tank rupture during qualification was traced to a manufacturing defect; cumulative program spend is approximately $360 million through end-2025. The stock closed near $78 in early May 2026 against a 52-week range of $20.23–$99.58.

ticker_iren.name: IREN Limited
ticker_iren.blurb: IREN Limited (formerly Iris Energy) is an Australian-founded, NASDAQ-listed company that began as a renewable-energy-powered bitcoin miner and has since pivoted aggressively toward AI and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure. The company controls significant power capacity — a scarce resource in the AI data-centre boom — across sites in North America, and rebranded from Iris Energy to IREN in November 2024 to signal the strategic shift.
ticker_iren.recent: IREN reported its first profitable fiscal year in 2025, with net income of $86.9 million on $501 million in revenue. A $9.7 billion, five-year cloud-computing agreement with Microsoft was signed in late 2025, calling for deployment of 76,000 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs across 200 megawatts at its Childress, Texas campus. The company targets scaling GPU capacity from 23,000 to 140,000 units through 2026, backed by 2,910 megawatts of renewable power infrastructure.

ticker_nbis.name: Nebius Group N.V.
ticker_nbis.blurb: Nebius Group is the Amsterdam-headquartered successor entity to Yandex's international operations after the Russian tech giant divested all domestic assets to a Russian consortium in a $5.4 billion transaction completed in July 2024. Led by Yandex co-founder Arkady Volozh, the renamed company has repositioned itself as a full-stack GPU cloud — a so-called neocloud — offering compute infrastructure for training and running large AI models. The Yandex engineering lineage gives it unusual depth in distributed systems and large-scale model serving.
ticker_nbis.recent: Nebius resumed NASDAQ trading under ticker NBIS in October 2024 (formerly YNDX). Revenue for fiscal 2025 came in at $529.8 million, up roughly 479% year-over-year. Management guided to $3.0-3.4 billion in 2026 revenue. A reported $2.7 billion infrastructure deal with Meta in early 2026 would represent a step-function expansion of its client base.

poster_mrmikeinvesting.blurb: A retail-focused stock-promotion account on X that publishes periodic lists of "top picks" — typically ten names spanning small-cap growth, AI-adjacent, and speculative sectors. The account presents itself as a stock and options trader and founder of "Mikes Trading." Posts are characterised by confident price targets, urgency framing ("don't miss out"), and recurring disclaimers that the author is not a financial adviser. The annual picks-list format — complete with claims of millionaire-making results from the prior year's edition — is a signature device. No audited track record is publicly available.
poster_mrmikeinvesting.credibility_note: The account makes unverifiable claims about returns from prior picks lists. Price targets are stated without disclosed methodology. The bottom portion of "top 10" lists is routinely withheld, a pattern common to accounts that monetise exclusivity through paid communities or follow-gating. Posts contain standard retail-influencer disclaimers. Treat all claims as promotional rather than analytical until independently verified.
